summary: Fourteen days of Nightscout CGM are complete enough for pattern review (98.7% coverage). Overall time in range is high (86.0%) with mean glucose 121.6 mg/dL, but time below range is 5.1% and clusters at local 01:00 and 19:00. Carbs were not logged, so meals were executed by always-on SMB and UAM rather than the CR table. The selected AAPS profile is treated as applicable. The only supported profile review after separating meal, IOB, and automation effects is raising the 00:00 target from 90 mg/dL to the already used 100 mg/dL daytime target, while holding basal, CR, ISF, DIA, and automation.

analysis_steps.findings: CGM quality is good: 3995 valid 5-minute points, 98.7% coverage, 10 gaps, largest gap 65 minutes, no invalid or duplicate points. Local timezone is BST. The selected AAPS profile is complete. Insulin telemetry is abundant (655 insulin entries, 275.95 U total), but the package includes only sampled treatments, loop statuses, and therapy windows. Carb entries are zero. A mid-period profile switch, site and sensor changes, an occlusion, GLP-1 notes, and temporary targets fragment some days. First and last calendar days are partial.
analysis_steps.evidence: Coverage 98.7% with expected cadence near 5 minutes; treatment summary shows 0 g carbs and about 19.7 U insulin per day; profile_context marks the selected profile historically applicable; representative events include the 13 Aug profile switch, site and sensor changes, 19 Aug occlusion, and GLP-1 notes.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No carb or e-carb records, no full IOB timeline, no activity stream, sampled rather than complete loop and treatment streams, u200 dilute unit scale not independently confirmed, strategy_stable_for_period is null.

analysis_steps.findings: Time below range 5.1% is the binding constraint despite strong time in range. Local 01:00 time-below-range is 18.5% with average 90.6 mg/dL and no time above range. Local 19:00 time-below-range is 15.3% with a minimum of 41 mg/dL. Other overnight hours near 23:00-03:00 also show about 10-11% time below range. Severe lows to 41-42 mg/dL and highs near 290 mg/dL both occur. Overnight averages sit on the 90 mg/dL target, leaving little hypo buffer. Sampled IOB reached about 4.7-5.9 U. Automation remains always-on SMB and UAM with Dynamic ISF and DIA 10 h.
analysis_steps.evidence: Glucose summary TIR 86.0%, TAR 8.9%, TBR 5.1%, CV 32.6%; local hourly rows for 00:00-03:00, 18:00-19:00, and 23:00; listed extremes on 13, 14, 15, 18, and 21 Aug; representative loop IOB peaks.
analysis_steps.dependencies: data_quality is sufficient for geography of highs and lows; missing carbs and incomplete IOB limit cause separation.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No rescue-carb or hypo-treatment log, incomplete IOB and activity, temporary targets and device faults around some extremes.

analysis_steps.findings: Overnight 00:00-04:00 scheduled basal is 0.6 U/h against a 90 mg/dL target, with averages near target and excess lows. Dawn 05:00-08:00 uses higher basal 0.7-0.8 U/h and is stable (time in range about 97-99%), so overnight lows are not a simple excess-basal signature. Daytime rise and 16:00 peak (average 162.8 mg/dL, 32.1% above range) coincide with unlogged intake and UAM lag, not a clean under-basal proof. The 16:00 basal cut to 0.5 U/h and the 19:00 rise to 0.7 U/h sit beside the 18:00-19:00 crash, so raising evening basal is unsupported. Loop zero-temps and high temps often override scheduled basal.
analysis_steps.evidence: Local hourly averages and time-below-range by clock hour; basal segments 0.6/0.7/0.8/0.7/0.5/0.6/0.7 U/h; targets 90 then 100 then 90 mg/dL; representative temp-basal zeros overnight and high daytime rates.
analysis_steps.dependencies: safety_overview makes time-below-range binding; meal and IOB effects were not excluded from daytime or evening windows.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No documented fasting challenge, sampled temps only, mid-window profile switch, site changes and occlusion can mimic basal error.

analysis_steps.findings: Five CR segments exist but were unused: zero carb entries and loop samples remain cob 0. Flat ISF 56 mg/dL/U matches the profile name, while Dynamic ISF produced much wider variable_sens values, so scheduled ISF is not the live correction factor. DIA 10 h can keep afternoon UAM insulin active into the 01:00 low cluster, but 4-6 h correction responses are mixed and do not isolate DIA. CR, ISF, and DIA therefore stay unchanged.
analysis_steps.evidence: Carb totals of 0 g; ISF segment 56 mg/dL/U; DIA 10 h; therapy windows are correction-only and inconsistent; sampled variable_sens roughly 28-124.
analysis_steps.dependencies: basal_targets overnight lows may be residual IOB rather than ISF or DIA error; safety_overview forbids stronger insulin while time-below-range is high.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No meal-linked CR tests, Dynamic ISF on, u200 scale, GLP-1 delayed absorption, sampled corrections only.

analysis_steps.findings: SMB and UAM are both enabled and SMB is always on, which matches zero COB and makes the unused cob/after-carb switches consistent rather than contradictory. High temporary-target SMB is off, so 135 mg/dL temporary targets are hypo-protective. Configured SMB interval is 3 minutes with 15-minute SMB and 20-minute UAM caps. Observed microboluses and UAM boosts were often larger than 15-20 minutes of scheduled basal and fit afternoon rise then 18:00-19:00 crash. Zero-temps appear after predicted lows, so protection is late. Delivery is a plausible later lever but is dependent on target, DIA, and Dynamic ISF, so it is held now.
analysis_steps.evidence: SMB settings always-on and UAM on; loop reasons with cob 0, 3-minute dosing, UAM boosts, and some 0.3-1.6 U SMBs; local 14:00-19:00 glucose pattern; high temporary targets on several afternoons.
analysis_steps.dependencies: safety_overview and unused CR from profile_cr_isf_dia; cannot treat UAM as duplicate COB counting.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Non-stock reason-string features, incomplete SMB time series, unknown dilution scale.

analysis_steps.findings: Autosens is off because autosens_enabled is false, not because many sensitivity_ratio values are 1. Dynamic ISF is on at 70% and is compensating for missing COB and a single daytime ISF, especially at highs when variable_sens fell near 28-38. Max IOB 25 U and max basal 12 U/h did not bind the observed lows; sampled IOB stayed near 5-6 U and some high temps clipped near 4 U/h. Carb-absorption settings are idle without logged carbs. No automation group is changed in this step.
analysis_steps.evidence: autosens_enabled false with Dynamic ISF true at 70%; sampled sensitivity_ratio values including 1 and some 0.79-0.98; max IOB 25 U versus sampled IOB 4.7-5.9 U; min_5m_carbimpact 8 and meal_max_absorption_hours 7 with 0 g carbs.
analysis_steps.dependencies: automation_smb_uam stack; profile ISF and DIA; safety_overview.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No full sensitivity history, GLP-1 effect on absorption not measured, u200 scale for caps.

analysis_steps.findings: User-declared meal_strategies is an empty list and strategy_stable_for_period is null, so no prebolus_minutes or immediate_bolus_percent exists to reproduce. Observed execution is UAM and SMB plus small corrections, not wizard meal boluses. Afternoon highs after tiny corrections and later crashes show delayed automation insulin, not a measured missed prebolus. Adding a full announced CR bolus on top of unchanged UAM would stack into the already high evening and overnight hypo risk.
analysis_steps.evidence: analysis_context meal_strategies empty; 0 carb treatments; 24 therapy windows all Correction Bolus with no extended carbs; local late-morning to afternoon rise and 19:00 crash.
analysis_steps.dependencies: CR unused; SMB/UAM always on; DIA 10 h; overnight target 90 mg/dL.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No declared prebolus or immediate bolus percent; no meal start times or grams.

analysis_steps.findings: No e-carb amounts, start offsets, or durations are present. E-carbs were not used and are not treated as pump extended boluses. Absorption settings cannot be judged from meal-linked evidence. GLP-1 notes can delay real absorption while UAM still doses a rise, but that is a hypothesis only.
analysis_steps.evidence: carb_treatment_entries empty; extended_carb_entries 0; therapy windows is_extended_carbs false; GLP-1 notes on 14, 17, and 20 Aug.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No meal composition and no e-carb duration evidence.

analysis_steps.findings: Ranked explanation for lows: overnight target 90 mg/dL with little buffer plus residual afternoon UAM/SMB and 10 h DIA, then possible Dynamic ISF over-correction at peaks, then less likely isolated overnight basal excess because dawn with higher basal is stable. Afternoon highs are unlogged intake and UAM lag, not a mandate to raise 10:00-16:00 or 19:00 basal. Conflicts resolved in favor of one hypo-protective profile lever: review 00:00 target 90 to 100 mg/dL, which already exists at 08:00. Hold 23:00 target, all basal, CR, ISF, DIA, and all six AAPS groups so dependent insulin-delivery settings are not moved together. Meal numeric strategy remains blocked until meal start and grams are logged.
analysis_steps.evidence: Local 01:00 time-below-range 18.5% with average 90.6 mg/dL and 0% above range; dawn stability on higher basal; zero carbs; Dynamic ISF and always-on UAM; decision inventory fully populated so AAPS verify is not available.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Unresolved u200 scale, plugin-like loop reasons, empty declared meal strategy, no fasting isolation of overnight basal.

strengths: CGM coverage is 98.7% with regular 5-minute cadence and no invalid points, so clock-time patterns are usable.
Overall time in range is 86.0% with mean glucose 121.6 mg/dL and coefficient of variation 32.6%.
Local 05:00-08:00 is stable on the higher dawn basal, with time in range about 97-99% and little time below range.
The selected profile is complete, historically marked applicable, and internally consistent with always-on SMB plus UAM when no carbs are logged.
Closed loop does issue zero-temps when predicted guard glucose collapses, showing late hypo protection is active.
issues: Time below range is 5.1%, with recurrent local 01:00 lows (18.5% below range, average 90.6 mg/dL on a 90 mg/dL target) and local 19:00 lows (15.3% below range, minimum 41 mg/dL).
Afternoon time above range peaks near 16:00 local without any carb announcements, so UAM and SMB are acting as the entire meal bolus.
Scheduled CR, e-carbs, and declared prebolus or immediate bolus percent cannot be checked because those fields are empty and Nightscout carbs are zero.
Dynamic ISF and frequent UAM SMBs can stack on DIA 10 h, which confounds overnight basal and scheduled ISF interpretation.
An occlusion, site changes, a mid-period profile switch, and GLP-1 notes add event-level noise around some extremes.

recommendations.title: Review raising only the 00:00 target from 90 to 100 mg/dL
recommendations.description: Local midnight-to-early-morning glucose sits on the 90 mg/dL target with substantial time below range and almost no time above range, while the 08:00 target is already 100 mg/dL and dawn basal is stable. This is the most separable hypo-protective profile review and does not require concluding that overnight basal is wrong.

recommendations.title: Hold basal and automation until that single target review is observed
recommendations.description: Afternoon highs and evening lows can be explained by unlogged meals plus UAM/SMB and Dynamic ISF. Changing 19:00 basal, SMB minutes, or Dynamic ISF in the same step would hide whether the 00:00 target review mattered.

profile_recommendation.recommendation: Review one profile value: 00:00 target 90 mg/dL to 100 mg/dL, matching the existing 08:00 target, and keep every basal, CR, ISF, DIA, and 23:00 target value unchanged during that review.
profile_recommendation.rationale: The strongest isolated overnight signal is time below range while average glucose sits on 90 mg/dL, especially at local 01:00, with 0% time above range in that hour. Higher scheduled basal after 05:00 is stable, so cutting overnight basal is not the first supported move. CR and meal insulin are unobservable. Scheduled ISF is overshadowed by Dynamic ISF. Raising only the 00:00 target uses an already present daytime target and reduces overnight insulin request without moving dependent delivery settings.
profile_recommendation.next_check: After this single 00:00 target review, compare several nights of local 01:00 and 23:00-03:00 time-below-range and average glucose without changing basal, DIA, SMB, or Dynamic ISF.

parameter_decisions.rationale: Evidence: local 00:00-03:00 time-below-range is high but averages are near 90-105 mg/dL, and 05:00-08:00 with higher basal is stable. Uncertainty: residual UAM IOB and DIA 10 h can mimic over-basal. Dependencies: the 00:00 target review; do not cut this basal in the same step.

Evidence: local 05:00-06:00 average about 104 mg/dL with high time in range and low time below range. Uncertainty: one 42 mg/dL reading near 07:19 local on 21 Aug is an outlier. Dependencies: overnight target observation first.

Evidence: local 06:00-08:00 remains in range with averages near 100-110 mg/dL despite this being the highest basal step. Uncertainty: partial last day and sensor change on 21 Aug. Dependencies: not a hypo-driver in the aggregate; hold while target is reviewed.

Evidence: late-morning rise and time above range occur with cob 0, which is more consistent with unlogged intake and UAM lag than under-basal. Uncertainty: no meal sizes. Dependencies: meal logging and unchanged UAM before any daytime basal increase.

Evidence: local 16:00 is the peak above-range hour, but 18:00-19:00 then crashes, so this lower basal may be protective rather than the cause of the peak. Uncertainty: meals, GLP-1, and UAM overlap this window. Dependencies: do not raise 16:00 basal while evening time-below-range is high.

Evidence: local 18:00 already has 7.7% time below range and a 42 mg/dL minimum. Uncertainty: this hour mixes residual afternoon SMB with possible evening intake. Dependencies: safety_overview; no evening basal increase.

Evidence: local 19:00 has 15.3% time below range and the period minimum of 41 mg/dL, so this step is poorly timed for an increase. Uncertainty: post-meal UAM versus scheduled basal cannot be fully split. Dependencies: hold this segment while target and later SMB questions are sequenced.
Evidence: zero carb entries and cob 0, so this CR was not used. Uncertainty: actual overnight intake unknown. Dependencies: meal start and gram logs before any CR review.
Evidence: no carb-linked breakfast or dawn meals to test 11.1 g/U. Uncertainty: unused table versus true need. Dependencies: carb logging; do not change CR with target.
Evidence: late-morning highs occurred without announced carbs, so UAM not CR produced the insulin. Uncertainty: meal composition unknown. Dependencies: blocked until grams are logged.
Evidence: afternoon peak then evening low is an automation-timing pattern, not a measured CR miss. Uncertainty: GLP-1 may delay absorption. Dependencies: no CR change on top of UAM.
Evidence: evening is a high time-below-range window with no carb records. Uncertainty: leftover IOB versus any late intake. Dependencies: hypo risk forbids tightening CR here first.

Evidence: Dynamic ISF is on and sampled variable_sens ranged far from 56, including about 28-38 at highs. Uncertainty: apparent strong corrections may be SMB stacking rather than a 56 error. Dependencies: do not retune scheduled ISF while Dynamic ISF, SMB, and the 00:00 target are being sequenced.

Evidence: local 00:00 average 93.3 mg/dL with 11.4% below range and 0% above; local 01:00 average 90.6 mg/dL with 18.5% below range and 0% above, all under this 90 mg/dL segment. Uncertainty: residual afternoon IOB may still cause lows at 100 mg/dL. Dependencies: keep basal, 23:00 target, DIA, SMB, and Dynamic ISF unchanged so this review is interpretable.

Evidence: this daytime target already provides more buffer than overnight 90 mg/dL and is the destination value for the 00:00 review. Uncertainty: afternoon highs are meal and UAM effects, not proof this target is too high. Dependencies: leave it unchanged while 00:00 is reviewed.

Evidence: local 23:00 average 105.7 mg/dL with 10.1% below range, but the densest lows are after 00:00. Uncertainty: the 23:00 start of 90 mg/dL may still contribute to the overnight descent. Dependencies: sequential review; revisit only if 23:00-00:00 time-below-range remains after the 00:00 target change.

Evidence: 10 h DIA can carry afternoon UAM into 01:00 lows, but 4-6 h correction windows both fall and rebound. Uncertainty: free_peak_oref peak and u200 dilution. Dependencies: changing DIA with target or SMB would confound IOB accounting.

Evidence: zero carbs means UAM is the meal engine; disabling it without a logged-meal path would leave afternoon highs untreated. Uncertainty: boost logic in loop reasons is not stock-simple. Dependencies: meal announcement strategy; not changed with the 00:00 target.

Evidence: always-on SMB makes unused cob switches consistent; high temporary-target SMB already off matches 135 mg/dL hypo-protective temporary targets. Uncertainty: how often those temporary targets actually suppressed SMB. Dependencies: keep high-TT SMB off while time-below-range is elevated.

parameter_decisions.current_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
parameter_decisions.suggested_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
parameter_decisions.rationale: Evidence: 3-minute UAM SMBs larger than 15-20 minutes of scheduled basal fit the afternoon rise and 19:00 crash. Uncertainty: non-stock boosts; remaining wait text is not the configured interval. Dependencies: observe the 00:00 target first; do not change delivery with Dynamic ISF or DIA.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS / max basal and max IOB limits
parameter_decisions.rationale: Evidence: sampled IOB peaked about 4.7-5.9 U, so 25 U did not cause the lows; some high temps clipped near 4 U/h rather than 12 U/h. Uncertainty: 25 U is a wide ceiling on a roughly 20 U/day total, especially with a u200 dilute label. Dependencies: ceiling discussion is separate from the target review and is not treated as the current mechanism.

Evidence: Autosens is disabled by autosens_enabled=false; a sensitivity_ratio of 1 is only a neutral current adjustment. Dynamic ISF at 70% is the live ISF and likely compensates for missing COB. Uncertainty: how much evening overshoot is Dynamic ISF versus SMB frequency. Dependencies: do not change this group with scheduled ISF, SMB minutes, or the 00:00 target.

Evidence: no carbs or e-carbs, so these settings did not drive COB. Uncertainty: they may matter only after logging starts, especially with GLP-1. Dependencies: meal records before any absorption-model review.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Keep the observed path: no declared prebolus, no immediate bolus percent, no e-carbs, and meals covered by already-on SMB and UAM. Do not add a full CR wizard bolus or e-carb stream on top of unchanged UAM.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: Declared meal_strategies is empty and Nightscout carbs are zero, so there is no prebolus, immediate percent, or e-carb value to apply. Telemetry shows afternoon rise and later 19:00 plus 01:00 lows from delayed UAM/SMB insulin, DIA 10 h, and a tight overnight target. A second full meal-insulin stream would stack on that IOB.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: For several typical daytime intakes, record only meal start time and carb grams while leaving profile and SMB settings unchanged.

exceptions.pattern: Same-day afternoon rise into local 18:00-20:00 and overnight 01:00
exceptions.suggestion: Do not add extra announced insulin or a larger immediate percent on top of UAM already delivered for that rise.
exceptions.rationale: This clock window has the highest time-below-range and the lowest recorded glucose, consistent with stacked automation insulin rather than a missed full bolus.

exceptions.pattern: High temporary target near 135 mg/dL, often around GLP-1 notes
exceptions.suggestion: Treat remaining rise in those windows as expected while high-TT SMB is off, not as a missed full immediate bolus.
exceptions.rationale: smb_with_high_temp_target_enabled is false, so those temporary targets are a hypo-protective exception rather than a second meal-dosing mode.

implementation_steps: Independently confirm the selected AAPS profile, the u200 dilute labeling, and that CGM coverage remains good before any setting review.
Discuss only the 00:00 target change from 90 mg/dL to 100 mg/dL with the care team; leave 23:00 target, all basal segments, CR, ISF, DIA, SMB, UAM, and Dynamic ISF untouched in that step.
If that single review is made, change it alone and watch local 01:00, 23:00-03:00, and 19:00 time-below-range plus overnight averages for several days.
In parallel, log meal start time and carb grams only, without adding a new bolus percentage or e-carb plan.
Only if overnight lows persist after the isolated 00:00 target review, reconsider one later lever: either the 23:00 target or SMB/UAM delivery, not both, and still without raising evening basal.
education: A target of 90 mg/dL with an overnight average near 90-93 mg/dL leaves little room for sensor noise, residual IOB, or delayed meals before glucose crosses below range.
When carbs are not logged, UAM is not a second carb counter; it is the meal bolus, so afternoon highs do not automatically mean scheduled basal or CR is too weak.
Dynamic ISF can make the live correction factor much stronger than a flat scheduled ISF of 56 mg/dL/U, which is why scheduled ISF and Dynamic ISF should not be judged or moved together.
A long DIA keeps earlier SMB insulin visible to the loop overnight, so evening and 01:00 lows can be leftover insulin rather than the 00:00 basal rate alone.
safety_notes: This is decision-support content only. The user must independently verify every proposed change, make changes one at a time, and monitor glucose closely.
TuneMyBG prepares data for review only and does not provide medical advice or automatically change AAPS.
Time below range of 5.1% and readings to 41-42 mg/dL are the binding safety limit for every later idea about basal, SMB, or meal insulin.
The profile name indicates u200 dilute insulin; unit scale was not independently verified, so all U/h and IOB figures should be confirmed against the pump and care team.
Occlusion, site changes, GLP-1 notes, and temporary targets can produce one-off extremes that should not be used as a single-point profile proof.
